case_title: Jasbir Singh v. Tarasingh and Others
mitigating_circumstances: Parties buying peace, parties settling the disputes and getting reconciled, victim subsequently becoming part of the family, victim showing interest in getting monetarily compensated, motive for commission of the crime, manner in which it was planned and committed
high_court_outcome: Reduced sentence to period already undergone
neutral_facts: The accused were tried for forging documents to grab the property of one Harbans Singh. The trial court imposed sentences ranging from 2 to 3 years of imprisonment and fines. The accused appealed, arguing that they were first offenders, faced prolonged trial, and had already undergone significant time in custody. The High Court reduced their sentences to the period already served. The Supreme Court remanded the matter back to the High Court for reconsideration, emphasizing that the appellate court should not arbitrarily reduce sentences without proper justification and that the factors leading to any reduction should be clearly stated.
